title: de.hubtask.automation.rule_run.finished.v1
description: An automation rule finished a run without failing: it acted, or its conditions said no, or a throttle held it back. One event for the three because they are one question with three answers, and `data.status` is which; a failure is its own type, so that an alert on rules failing does not have to filter a field to avoid firing on rules working. The wire format is a CloudEvent 1.0 in structured JSON (ADR-0007); the tenant, the actor and the causal chain travel as CloudEvents extension attributes, whose names are lower case without separators as the specification requires. Single-value enums stand in for `const`, and the bounds of a value are stated in its description rather than as keywords: the contract test validates against this file with the subset of JSON Schema the project implements, and a keyword it silently ignored would be a promise nobody checks. Fields may be added; removing or reinterpreting one requires a .v2 delivered alongside .v1 for at least two minor releases (domain-model.md §4).

id.description: UUIDv7. Stable across delivery attempts, so a consumer deduplicates on it (at-least-once delivery).

source.description: The installation and the bounded context that produced the event.

subject.description: `rule_run/<id>` - the run, which is what a consumer looks the rest up by.

actorid.description: Absent when the system itself acts. No label: an event leaves the installation, and a name is personal data a subscriber does not need in order to react (ADR-0018).

onbehalfof.description: The principal an automation rule or an agent runs as.

correlationid.description: Everything that came out of one original action carries the same value. A root event is its own correlation.

causationid.description: The event that caused this one. Absent for an action a person took.

causationdepth.description: Distance from the original action. The rule engine stops at 5 and marks the run ABORTED_LOOP (automation.md §2).

rule_id.description: The rule the run belongs to.

event_id.description: The event that started the run, when one did.

causation_depth.description: How far this run is from the act a person performed. The engine aborts at the documented limit rather than following the chain further (automation.md §2).

status.description: SUCCEEDED acted, SKIPPED had a condition answer false, THROTTLED was held back by the rule's own bound.

actions_succeeded.description: How many actions ran and did what they say.

actions_failed.description: How many ran and refused. Non-zero here with `SUCCEEDED` is `on_error: CONTINUE` doing what it says.
